          Model routing

          Who answers the assistant, and how each task's model is chosen. Ready routes list first; the rest stay selectable and can be set up later. Models are saved per provider, so switching never mixes them.

          The stages behind these switches — who checks the ask, who plans it, who briefs it, when Jev is asked and who picks the model — are drawn as a graph in . Making a map live moves the switches its parts name.

          Who answers

          Auto order
            The first ready provider answers. With fallback on, a failed or keyless HTTP route retries down the list.

            Models & selection

            Model selection

            Checking model selection…

            No selection recorded yet.

            How Jev chooses

            Jev ranks the models within your chosen provider for each task by catalog quality, estimated price, and your project's measured timing, errors, ratings and reported costs; missing evidence stays unknown. Each selection is one small billed gateway request and needs a Jev key (below); when Jev is unavailable the usual default runs. Model overrides always win. CLI routes use their saved model or CLI default; LM Studio and custom endpoints answer with the model loaded at their URL unless you save an override.

            Coding workers

            Workers carry out queued tasks in your selected project. Pick a builder whose CLI is installed and signed in, then what each build may cost.

            Builder

            How tiers resolve

            Tier models are saved per CLI. A tier without a model of its own uses Studio's default for that CLI or the CLI's own default; Free never falls back to a billed model. Auto lets Jev or the stand-in judge pick per task within your provider, and a pinned model wins.

            Coding tier

            Checking coding tiers…

            JevTask-aware model selection and optional task suggestions

            Choose where Jev is routed: the Vercel AI Gateway, TypeSafe's Jev API directly, OpenCode Zen (including its free Jev tier), or OpenRouter. Each route keeps its own key, stored encrypted; switching never moves a key between routes. The key connects Jev for model selection above and optional task suggestions. Intake classification compares incoming work with existing tasks and records suggestions; its switch does not change model selection.

            Checking Jev…

            Providers, model routing, coding workers and Jev connect through the desktop app. Run npm start in mefi-studio, or open the portable app, to set them up.

            Linking reads your Discord id and name, and your roles and join date in the Void Engine server: when you link, about once a week (sooner after a failed check, then daily), and when you press Check now.                       Agents

                      How your agents run the queue. Changes apply to every project and never interrupt work already in progress.

                      Autopilot… Workers… Mode…

                      Queue

                      Starts ready tasks and verifies what comes back. Off stops new starts; running jobs finish.
                      How many builds run at once. Machine managed backs off while the machine is busy.
                      Auto build starts eligible tasks itself. Verify first holds each new or changed brief for your approval.
                      Both modes collaborate and delegate subtasks. Swarm works across the queue; Cluster focuses on one shared task.

                      Safety

                      Stop all halts every agent now; progress is saved and the work stays queued. Restart stops the agents first, then relaunches Studio paused.

                      About these controls
                      Autopilot
                      The master switch for the assistant's queue. On each pass the assistant looks for ready tasks, starts them while a worker slot is free, and verifies what came back. Turning it off stops new work from starting; jobs already running finish normally.
                      Parallel builds
                      How many builds may run at the same time. Machine managed starts work while the app stays responsive and backs off when the machine is busy. A manual limit (1–3) caps concurrent builds but never starts or pauses anything by itself.
                      Build mode
                      Auto build starts eligible tasks as soon as a worker is free. Verify first holds every new or changed brief for your approval, so you decide what gets built. Switching never interrupts a running job.
                      Agent mode
                      How agents coordinate. Swarm works across all ready tasks and their subtasks; Cluster focuses every agent on one shared task until it is done. Both plan, delegate and review results; current work finishes when you switch. The same selector sits in the node tree toolbar under Agents for quick changes.
                      New work
                      The master switch for starting anything new — queued tasks, builds and work the assistant suggests — lives with the Assistant. Off pauses admission; running jobs, replies and your answers to questions still work.

                      Done

                      Loading…

                      Builds that finished, from the durable executor ledger. Done means the worker reported success; Failed means it stopped early. A finished node collapses into its host on the tree; its brief stays readable on that card.

                                      What the marks mean

                                      • Colour is the stage a part belongs to: intake, checks, planning, assistant, routing, build, decisions. A wire takes the colour of the part it leaves.
                                      • Map rulesThe map itself decides here. Editing it changes behaviour as soon as the map is saved.
                                      • NoteA drawing only: saved and shown, but nothing runs it.
                                      • Moves a real switch when the map goes live. Every other part holds settings for a stage the studio already runs.
                                      • A dashed wire is a feedback wire: what it carries lands on the next pass.
                                      • A red ring is a required end with nothing wired, and a red part or wire is a problem to fix before the map can go live.
                                      Settings · Diagnostics

                                      Performance profiler

                                      Ready to record

                                      Start a capture, close this panel, and reproduce the slowdown. Return here to stop, inspect and export.

                                      Frame history latest 180 UI intervals

                                      Rendering hotspots ranked by total self time

                                      Self time excludes nested measured work. A high average or p95 identifies consistently expensive operations; a high maximum reveals a spike.

                                      OperationCallsSelf totalSelf / callMeanp95Worst

                                      Host requests ranked by total elapsed time

                                      These durations include asynchronous waiting and can overlap. A slow request is not necessarily a blocked UI or high CPU usage.

                                      RequestCallsMeanp95WorstErrors

                                      Recent hitches

                                      Nearby scopes help locate a slowdown; they do not prove its cause. Frame gaps, long tasks and scope events may describe the same hitch.

                                        Studio processes

                                        ProcessCPUMemory

                                        Memory is each process's working set. Shared pages may be counted in more than one process.

                                        Capture stays in memory until you export. Reports contain operation names and measurements, with no task text, request payloads, paths or credentials. Profiling adds some measurement overhead.
